title: Align password setup and changes with NIST SP 800-63B-4
body:
Password creation and password changes currently use different validation, and the password-change composition rules reject long passphrases that meet the length recommendation in NIST SP 800-63B-4.

Verified against upstream main at `fcc18b392f44e67d1fac6d676b0b39742d3b3cff`.

Observed source behaviour:
- [`core/archipelago/src/api/rpc/auth.rs`](https://source.archipelago-foundation.org/lfg2025/archy/src/commit/fcc18b392f44e67d1fac6d676b0b39742d3b3cff/core/archipelago/src/api/rpc/auth.rs), `handle_auth_setup`: requires a minimum of eight UTF-8 bytes without making MFA compulsory for setup.
- [`core/archipelago/src/auth.rs`](https://source.archipelago-foundation.org/lfg2025/archy/src/commit/fcc18b392f44e67d1fac6d676b0b39742d3b3cff/core/archipelago/src/auth.rs), `validate_password_strength`: requires at least 12 UTF-8 bytes plus uppercase, lowercase, digit and special-character checks.
- Both length checks use `str::len()`, which counts UTF-8 bytes, so the stated character minimum differs for non-ASCII input.

Example: a synthetic passphrase such as `quiet orchard lantern` is over 15 characters but the change-password validator rejects it for missing an uppercase letter, digit and symbol. It is not a real account password.

Suggested outcome:
1. Use one shared password policy across setup and password changes.
2. Remove mandatory mixtures of character classes; accept long passphrases and spaces.
3. Require at least 15 characters where a password can be used alone. An eight-character minimum is an option only where password use is exclusively part of MFA; handle disabling/recovering MFA consistently.
4. Count Unicode code points rather than UTF-8 bytes when enforcing character length.
5. Include long-passphrase and Unicode regression cases. Assess common/compromised-password screening as part of the shared validator; this report does not claim a complete authentication audit.

Reference: [NIST SP 800-63B-4, section 3.1.1.2](https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-4/sp800-63b/authenticators/#passwordver). This is a request to align password-policy behaviour with that guidance, not a claim about Archy's overall NIST compliance or a legal obligation.

Related: [#126 — Password missing a special character crashes out](https://source.archipelago-foundation.org/lfg2025/archy/issues/126) is closed and concerns error handling; this report concerns the policy and consistency themselves.
